references.text: God tells Moses that He will lay His hand on Egypt and bring His people out with great judgments, a direct fulfillment of the promise in Gen 15:14 to judge the nation they were serving.

God tells Moses that when the Israelites leave Egypt, they will not go empty-handed but will ask for silver, gold, and clothing from the Egyptians—a fulfillment of the promise to depart with great wealth.
God promises to free the Israelites from slavery in Egypt and lead them out with a mighty hand and great judgments, reflecting the promise of judgment in Gen 15:14.

The Israelites asked the Egyptians for silver, gold, and clothing, and the Lord gave them favor in the eyes of the Egyptians—the direct fulfillment of the promise that they would depart with great wealth.
The psalmist describes how God brought Israel out with silver and gold, and Egypt was glad when they left—a poetic account of the fulfillment of the promise in Gen 15:14.
Theological parallel: The principle that God's people are freed after their oppressor has received judgment.
Direct quote and fulfillment: Luke confirms the prophecy from Genesis 15:14 as a historical event.
